multiplechoiceresponse.p: In a table, one row should represent:

choice.div: One observation — one record of the thing being measured.
A summary total for the column.

div.p: Rows are observations, columns are variables. Mixing a totals row in with the observations breaks SUM, filters and pivots.

choice.div: One row per observation, one column per variable, no totals interleaved.
Two merged header rows and a subtotal every ten rows.
A single column holding "name, region, and date joined".

div.p: Tidy data is what every later tool assumes. Merged headers, interleaved totals and multi-fact columns all break filtering, pivoting and SQL.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: A column of revenue values will not sum. The most likely cause is:

choice.div: The numbers are stored as text (often with stray spaces or a currency symbol).
The sheet has too many rows.
The column needs to be sorted first.

div.p: Text-formatted numbers sort and calculate wrongly and silently. Convert the column — and check for the whitespace or symbol that caused it.
